articles.title: Phillips' 107 Powers New Zealand to Record 259/7 and 87-Run Win Over India
articles.excerpt: Glenn Phillips smashed 107 off 49 balls and Michael Bracewell 65 off 25 as New Zealand posted their highest-ever T20I total — and the highest against India — before Jacob Duffy's 4/23 sealed an 87-run win in the fourth T20I at Eden Park. India still lead the series 3-1.
articles.nri_angle: India's first defeat of the series came in front of a sold-out Eden Park crowd with a large Indian diaspora presence; the fifth and final T20I now decides whether India close the tour 4-1 or 3-2.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sold-Out Eden Park Crowd to Break New Zealand Bilateral Record for India T20I
articles.excerpt: Nearly 40,000 fans will watch Friday's fourth T20I in Auckland, passing the 36,523 mark set in 2019 — for a series India have already won.
articles.image_caption: Beautiful panorama of Eden Park stadium in Auckland, New Zealand, photographed by Kiwi Flickr. Friday's fourth T20I between New Zealand and India at Eden Park is sold out, with nearly 40,000 fans expected in Auckland.
articles.image_credit: Photo: This image's author is Kiwi Flickr Attribution — You must give appropriate credi via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
articles.nri_angle: A record Eden Park crowd for an India match shows the diaspora-driven commercial pull of Indian cricket in New Zealand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Josh Inglis Makes Australian History With Comeback Test Century in Cape Town Decider
articles.excerpt: Recalled at short notice after a finger injury, Inglis scored 102 off 135 balls against South Africa at Newlands to become the first Australian with multiple centuries in all three international formats.
articles.image_caption: Josh Inglis raises his bat and helmet to celebrate his century against South Africa at Newlands in Cape Town. His 102 made him the first Australian with multiple centuries in all three international formats.
articles.nri_angle: Indian fans know Inglis from the IPL — Punjab Kings signed him for Rs 2.60 crore in 2025 and Lucknow Super Giants paid Rs 8.6 crore for him at the IPL 2026 mini-auction.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: At 15, Uma Kashvi Becomes Youngest Player Ever Signed in WPL Auction
articles.excerpt: Delhi Capitals bought the Karnataka all-rounder for Rs 10 lakh in Kochi — 15 years and 202 days old, with an Under-15 average of 172 behind her.
articles.nri_angle: The WPL's youngest signing is a window on how early India's women's cricket pipeline now identifies and contracts talent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UP Warriorz Sign Sophie Molineux for Rs 1.10 Crore at WPL Auction
articles.excerpt: Australia's captain was the costliest buy in Kochi as UP Warriorz filled all eight open slots, brought back Grace Harris, and beat RCB in the day's biggest bidding contest.
articles.image_caption: Australian cricketer Sophie Molineux, signed by UP Warriorz for Rs 1.10 crore at the WPL auction
articles.nri_angle: The WPL auction shapes the squads Indian and diaspora cricket fans will follow when the league's fifth season starts in January.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pramanik's Eight Wickets Put Bengal Six Wickets From Third Straight Ranji Win
articles.excerpt: Left-arm spinner Pradipta Pramanik took four wickets in each innings as Bengal bowled Kerala out for 141, set a target of 409 and reduced the hosts to 53 for 4 by the close of day three in Thiruvananthapuram.
articles.nri_angle: Ranji Trophy form from players such as Mohammed Shami shapes India's Test selection debates followed closely by diaspora cricket fans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Arshdeep Singh Breaks Bhuvneshwar Record With 38 T20I Wickets in 2026
articles.excerpt: The left-arm seamer's 2 for 33 against New Zealand in Christchurch took him past Bhuvneshwar Kumar's 37 wickets in 2022, in 26 innings, and level with Wanindu Hasaranga in the full-member list.
articles.image_caption: Arshdeep Singh playing for India at the MCG during the 2022 T20 World Cup (Wikimedia Commons).
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora fans following India's New Zealand tour, Arshdeep's next matches carry a second storyline: two more wickets would make him the outright full-member record holder for T20I wickets in a calendar year.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.excerpt: F4 Round 4 and Indian Racing League Round 2 run at Greater Noida on October 31 and November 1, with Luviwe Sambudla leading the F4 standings on 138 points.
articles.nri_angle: The return of FIA-level racing to India's former F1 circuit is a home-country motorsport milestone for diaspora fans who follow Indian racing, and the Delhi-NCR venue makes it accessible to families visiting India during the festival season.

articles.title: Mandeep Singh Hat-Trick Powers India To 13-0 Rout Of Bangladesh In Jalandhar
articles.excerpt: Harmanpreet, Dilpreet and Hardik scored twice each as the defending champions led 6-0 at half-time in their Asian Champions Trophy opener on October 27.
articles.nri_angle: A home tournament in Punjab, with Jalandhar players including Harmanpreet and Mandeep central to the win, connects directly to Punjabi diaspora families in Canada, the US and the UK who follow Indian hockey closely.

articles.title: Ashes and India Series Power Cricket Australia to Record A$601 Million Revenue
articles.excerpt: A home Ashes and India's white-ball tour turned an A$11.3 million loss into an A$81.8 million surplus, even as two-day Tests cost CA A$20 million and lean years loom.
articles.image_caption: Australian players celebrate a wicket during a Test match. Cricket Australia reported record revenue of A$601.1 million and an A$81.8 million surplus for 2025-26, driven by the Ashes and India's white-ball tour.
articles.nri_angle: India's white-ball tour was one of the two properties that produced Cricket Australia's record year, underlining the commercial weight Indian and diaspora audiences carry in world cricket.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bhuvneshwar Says He Never Chased a Comeback After Four Years Out
articles.excerpt: Back in India's T20I side for the first time since November 2022, 36-year-old Bhuvneshwar Kumar credited two strong IPL seasons, said he will play the Vijay Hazare and Syed Mushtaq Ali trophies, and insisted a bowler can still control a T20 game.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Badoni's Back-to-Back Double Centuries Put Him Alongside Kohli and Gambhir
articles.excerpt: Delhi captain Ayush Badoni followed his 217 against Gujarat with an unbeaten 210 against Jharkhand in Ranchi, becoming the 21st Indian batter to score double centuries in consecutive first-class innings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Abhishek Sharma's 113 Off 38 Balls Seals Series for India
articles.excerpt: India chased 199 in 13.2 overs in Wellington, beating New Zealand by six wickets with a record 118-run powerplay to lead 3-0.
articles.image_caption: Indian cricketer Abhishek Sharma. Sharma's 113 off 38 balls sealed the series for India.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora cricket fans, a 15-year-old opener and a 35-ball century in Wellington is the India T20 side's next generation arriving at once.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: South Africa Faces Australia in Crucial ODI at Newlands
articles.excerpt: The two cricketing giants clash in a pivotal ODI match today.

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ICC Moves Into WADA's Top Compliance Tier Ahead of Cricket's Olympic Return
articles.excerpt: WADA upgraded the ICC from tier 2 to tier 1 from January 1 because of cricket's Olympic inclusion, putting cricket under the strictest compliance monitoring — timely testing, whereabouts pursuit and three-month deadlines to fix critical failures.
articles.nri_angle: India remains in the top tier of national signatories too, so Indian cricketers face the strictest testing regime into LA 2028.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Raina Sees Dhoni-Yuvraj Quality in Tilak Varma After Record Christchurch Chase
articles.excerpt: Suresh Raina compared Tilak Varma to MS Dhoni and Yuvraj Singh after Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy chased 68 off the last five overs to beat New Zealand and take a 2-0 series lead.
articles.image_caption: India batter Tilak Varma. Suresh Raina compared Varma's middle-order temperament to MS Dhoni and Yuvraj Singh after his unbeaten stand with Nitish Kumar Reddy won the second T20I against New Zealand in Christchurch.
articles.nri_angle: India's T20I series in New Zealand is prime viewing for the diaspora in both countries, and Varma's emergence gives the touring side a new finisher to follow.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Eye Series Seal As Wellington Wind Tests Bowlers In Third T20I
articles.excerpt: Leading 2-0 after two Christchurch wins, India can close out the five-match series on Tuesday — if they handle Hnry Stadium's 55 kph gusts, short square boundaries and New Zealand's spinners.
articles.image_caption: Image: @cricinfo via X
articles.nri_angle: For Indian fans in New Zealand and the wider diaspora, a series-clinching win in Wellington would extend India's hold over the World Cup runners-up on their own soil.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Lose 1-6 to Senegal and Drop Into Tier C at FIFA U15 Festival
articles.excerpt: Abdoulaye Diallo scored four goals as Senegal overran the previously unbeaten Blue Colts in Baku, leaving India third in Group K and playing for positions 65th to 96th in the tournament stage.
articles.image_caption: India's under-15 team lines up before a match at the FIFA U15 World Cup and Festival in Baku. India dropped into Tier C after a 1-6 defeat to Senegal in their final group match.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families following Indian youth football, India's Tier C placement matches from October 28 offer further televised minutes for the Blue Colts despite the group-stage exit from Tier A contention.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Why New Zealand Cannot Crack India's Death Bowling in T20I Series
articles.excerpt: Bracewell cites 26 and 23 runs conceded in the last two overs of the Christchurch matches as India lead 2-0, with Wellington now a must-win for the hosts.
articles.image_caption: India pacer Arshdeep Singh, who took 2 for 33 in the second T20I in Christchurch as India's death bowling restricted New Zealand again.
articles.nri_angle: India's late-overs control in New Zealand, in a series decided by fine margins in Christchurch, is the phase diaspora fans will watch first in the Wellington must-win match.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ishan Kishan Ruled Out of Wellington T20I Despite Recovering Well
articles.excerpt: The BCCI says Kishan is recovering from a low-grade right adductor strain but has not regained match fitness for the October 27 third T20I.
articles.nri_angle: Indian cricket fans in New Zealand and worldwide will miss Kishan in Wellington as India chase a series-sealing win.

articles.title: 'Ticking Bomb': Ex-Coach Reveals Rohit Sharma's Career-Threatening 2017 Hip Injury
articles.excerpt: Former India S&C coach Soham Desai says Rohit has managed a surgically repaired hip since the 2017 Champions Trophy, needing two strength sessions a week to keep playing at 39.
articles.image_caption: India captain Rohit Sharma (file photo)
articles.nri_angle: Rohit Sharma remains the biggest draw in Indian cricket for diaspora fans, and his fitness will decide whether they see him at one last ODI World Cup in 2027.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Have Bulletproof Workload Plan for New Zealand Tour, Morkel Says
articles.excerpt: With the first Test starting four days after the ODI series ends, India will keep a cover group of bowlers in New Zealand — and Arshdeep Singh is in the conversation for a Test debut.
articles.nri_angle: India's New Zealand tour is a major live-cricket draw for the large Indian diaspora in New Zealand and for US and UK fans following the series across time zones.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shadab Khan's Maiden Century Drags Pakistan From 154 for 9 to One-Wicket Win Over England
articles.excerpt: Batting at No. 8, Shadab made an unbeaten 113 and shared a record 89-run tenth-wicket stand with Haris Rauf in Lahore. Pakistan reached the tri-series final; England lost their third match in a row.
articles.image_caption: Pakistan batsmen Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf run between the wickets during the ODI tri-series match against England in Lahore. Their unbroken 89-run tenth-wicket stand took Pakistan from 154 for 9 to a one-wicket win.
articles.nri_angle: A record last-wicket ODI heist is appointment viewing for South Asian cricket fans across the diaspora, and it reshapes the tri-series England must now survive.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ahmedabad to Host 2029 World Weightlifting Championships, a First for India
articles.excerpt: The IWF Executive Board picked Ahmedabad over bids linked to Russia and Venezuela; the championships will double as a qualifying event for the 2030 Commonwealth Games.
articles.image_caption: A weightlifter in competition (file image). Ahmedabad will host the 2029 IWF World Weightlifting Championships, a first for India.
articles.nri_angle: Ahmedabad adds the weightlifting worlds to its 2030 Commonwealth Games programme, another global event in India for diaspora fans planning home trips around sport.

articles.title: Rahane Picks Bumrah-Led Five-Man Pace Attack for 2027 World Cup, Leaves Out Shami
articles.excerpt: Rahane chose Bumrah, Arshdeep, Prasidh, Siraj and the uncapped-in-ODIs Mayank Yadav on Sony Sports — omitting World Cup record wicket-taker Mohammed Shami, Harshit Rana and Bhuvneshwar Kumar.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora cricket fans debating India's 2027 World Cup squad get Rahane's exact five and the case for and against omitting Shami.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: KL Rahul Out Hit Wicket for Four After Duck as India A Fight Back in Lincoln
articles.excerpt: Rahul was dismissed by Fraser Sheat twice — edging behind for a duck, then hitting his own stumps trying to stop a rolling ball — while Padikkal and Sudharsan took India A to 106 for 2, trailing New Zealand A by 98.
articles.nri_angle: Indian cricket fans abroad following Rahul's red-ball form ahead of the senior New Zealand Test series get the full score context, not just the viral dismissal.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dhoni to Decide on IPL 2027 Before December, With Fitness Tests to Settle CSK Return
articles.excerpt: The 45-year-old missed the entire IPL 2026 season with a calf injury. At a Bengaluru event he put the decision on his medical report, while CSK's chief executive said the call is Dhoni's alone.
articles.image_caption: MS Dhoni bats in Chennai Super Kings colours during an IPL match. Dhoni said he will decide before December, based on medical test results, whether he is fit to play another IPL season in 2027.
articles.nri_angle: Dhoni's decision, due before December, determines whether diaspora IPL fans get one final season of the league's defining captain in CSK colours in 2027.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's 300th T20I Brings a First: 200 Outright Wins in the Format
articles.excerpt: Saturday's four-wicket win over New Zealand in Christchurch was India's 300th men's T20I and their 200th outright win — a landmark reached in a format they first played, almost as an experiment, in December 2006.
articles.image_caption: YouTube / Feild Stats
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora fans who have followed India's T20 rise from the 2007 Johannesburg final onward, the 300-match mark closes a two-decade arc from novelty format to India's most dominant one.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tilak's Unbeaten 51 Rescues India in Last-Over Thriller Against New Zealand
articles.excerpt: India recovered from 70 for 5 and 112 for 6 to chase 181 with one ball to spare at Hagley Oval, taking a 2-0 lead in the five-match T20I series.
articles.nri_angle: India's young middle order produced a record seventh-wicket stand to give diaspora fans a 2-0 series lead to savour.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Former MLB Stars Find Cricket Skills Transfer Fast at Mumbai Kids Clinic
articles.excerpt: Nick Swisher, Adrian Gonzalez and Jake Arrieta coached Hansraj Morarji School students in Mumbai, said the girls outperformed the boys, and pointed to Saturday's MLBx showdown with India's cricketers.
articles.image_caption: Nick Swisher in a file photograph. The former MLB star joined Adrian Gonzalez and Jake Arrieta at a baseball clinic for Mumbai school students on October 23.
articles.nri_angle: American baseball legends coaching Mumbai schoolchildren, then facing India's cricketers at MLBx, is a direct US-India sporting crossover for diaspora fans of both games.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pankaj Advani Beats Robert Hall to Win 29th World Title in Billiards
articles.excerpt: Trailing by more than 300 points in the World Billiards Championship final, Pankaj Advani produced a championship-high 587 break to beat Robert Hall 1906-1206 and claim his 29th career world title.
articles.image_caption: Pankaj Advani holds the John Roberts Trophy after winning the World Billiards Championship. The Bengaluru cueist beat England's Robert Hall 1906-1206 in the final to claim his 29th world title.
articles.nri_angle: Advani's win in England extends India's dominance in cue sports, a title run followed closely by Indian sports fans worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Harmeet Desai, Yashaswini Ghorpade End India's 72-Year Mixed Doubles Wait
articles.excerpt: The Indian pair beat South Korea in a five-game quarter-final in Tashkent and took bronze at the Asian Table Tennis Championships, India's first mixed doubles medal since 1954.
articles.image_caption: Harmeet Desai and Yashaswini Ghorpade hold trophies on a World Table Tennis podium. The pair won bronze in mixed doubles at the Asian Table Tennis Championships in Tashkent, India's first medal in the event in 72 years.
articles.nri_angle: A historic continental medal for Indian table tennis, ending a 72-year wait in mixed doubles, is a landmark result for Indian sport followed closely by diaspora fans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rawal's Unbeaten Century Powers India to Nine-Wicket Win Over Zimbabwe in Opener
articles.excerpt: Pratika Rawal made 100 not out and Shafali Verma smashed 64 not out from 33 balls as India chased 198 in 27.1 overs in Vadodara, after Shree Charani's 4 for 23 restricted Zimbabwe to 197 in the first ODI of a new three-match series.
articles.nri_angle: India's women opened a new home ODI series with a dominant win, led by a century from Pratika Rawal — a result diaspora cricket fans can follow through the remaining matches on October 25 and 28 in Vadodara.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
